synthesisRows.use: Computational drug-repurposing hypothesis for anti-TNF-refractory Crohn disease

finding.text: Vorinostat was nominated by an original computational analysis of Crohn disease transcriptomes. The result identifies a hypothesis for experimental testing and does not demonstrate symptom improvement, remission or clinical safety.

synthesisRows.magnitudeText: CMap enrichment score 12.3, cluster 1. This is a computational score, not a clinical effect size; a clinical effect interval is not identifiable from this design.
synthesisRows.evidenceBase: One original computational analysis; the source describes transcriptomes from 327 patients, with no new intervention cohort. Both Crohn candidate rows belong to this same analysis.

limitations.text: The analysis used one transcriptome dataset; the authors note potential selection bias and the need for experimental confirmation.
Candidate nomination cannot quantify patient benefit, and neither drug was tested as a Crohn treatment in this report.
